title: Nehemiah 2
paragraphs: ¹ In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, wine was brought before him, and I took the wine and presented it to the king. I had not been sad in his presence before, ² so the king asked me, "Why does your face look so sad? You don't appear to be sick — this must be sadness of heart." I was very frightened. ³ I said to the king, "May the king live forever! How could my face not look sad when the city where my ancestors are buried lies in ruins and its gates have been destroyed by fire?" ⁴ The king asked me, "What are you asking for?" I prayed to the God of heaven ⁵ and then answered the king, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, send me to Judah, to the city where my ancestors are buried, so that I may rebuild it."

⁶ The king, with the queen seated beside him, asked me, "How long will the journey take, and when will you return?" It pleased the king to send me, and I gave him a time. ⁷ I also said to the king, "If it pleases the king, let him give me letters to the governors of the region beyond the Euphrates, so that they will let me pass through until I reach Judah. ⁸ And let him give me a letter to Asaph, keeper of the royal forest, so he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel by the temple, for the city wall, and for the house where I will live." The king granted my requests, for God's gracious hand was on me. ⁹ When I came to the governors of the region beyond the Euphrates, I gave them the king's letters. The king had sent army officers and cavalry with me. ¹⁰ But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about this, they were deeply disturbed that someone had come to seek the welfare of the Israelites.

¹¹ I went to Jerusalem and stayed there three days. ¹² Then I set out at night with a few men. I had not told anyone what God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem. There was no animal with me except the one I was riding. ¹³ By night I went out through the Valley Gate, past the Dragon Spring toward the Dung Gate, inspecting the walls of Jerusalem, which had been broken down, and its gates, which had been consumed by fire. ¹⁴ Then I moved on to the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was not enough room for my animal to pass. ¹⁵ So I went up by the valley in the night and inspected the wall before turning back and entering through the Valley Gate.

¹⁶ The officials had no idea where I had gone or what I was doing; I had not yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or any of the others who would be doing the work. ¹⁷ Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in — Jerusalem lies in ruins and its gates have been burned down. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem so we will no longer be in disgrace." ¹⁸ I also told them how God's gracious hand had been upon me and what the king had said to me. They replied, "Let us start rebuilding." So they committed themselves to this good work. ¹⁹ But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they mocked and ridiculed us. "What is this you are doing?" they asked. "Are you rebelling against the king?" ²⁰ I answered them, "The God of heaven will grant us success. We his servants will start rebuilding. But you have no share in Jerusalem, no claim, and no historic right to it."
